title: VM1 motion-state backtest harness (out-of-band, no production changes)
summary: Operator hypothesis: VM1's prompt currently asserts the subject is moving, so when a parked car appears in a tree-wind motion bbox, VM1 returns the parked car as 'the moving subject' and the matcher fires TG#2/3. To test, build a STANDALONE backtest harness that takes yesterday's alert fixtures (frame_002, frame_003, composite) and re-feeds them through a NEW VM1 prompt that asks: (a) what class is moving, (b) bbox in frame_2 coords, (c) bbox in frame_3 coords. Render VM1's bboxes on the composite for operator review. NO production code changes; the backtest is offline-only.
operator_provided_problem: Alert 15:15:59 EDT 2026-09-30 OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE: tree motion triggered Reolink MD, YOLO found operator Tesla Model Y at the edge of the motion bbox, VM1 said 'blue car parked on gravel, partially visible', matcher hit v_darkblue_tesla_y_operator, TG#2 fired with 'Class confirmed: Tesla'.

Alert 13:13:45 EDT 2026-09-30 OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR: tree motion triggered Reolink MD, YOLO found helper Silverado at lower-left corner of crop, VM2 said 'white Chevrolet pickup truck visible in the lower left corner of the image, parked on a gravel surface near a line of tall pine trees', match hit v_white_silverado_helper_a, TG#2 fired.

Both alerts: the vehicle did not move. Only the trees moved. Reolink fired alarm.type=vehicle because its AI detected the parked vehicle while tree motion triggered the MD. Current system has no way to distinguish 'parked car + tree motion' from 'car drove in'.
VM1 prompt line 79 of infra/vm1_prompt.py: 'The crops show one moving subject.' This pre-asserts motion; VM1 cannot return 'stationary' even when the subject is parked.

in_scope: Re-render composite.png from existing frame_001..frame_004 + diff (uses infra/motion_visualization.py)
Build a NEW prompt module: infra/backtest_vm1_prompt.py (NOT infra/vm1_prompt.py, which is production)
Send 3 images to local vision model: frame_002, frame_003, composite_with_red_overlay
Prompt asks: class (vehicle/person/animal/unsure), bbox in frame_2 native coords, bbox in frame_3 native coords
Render VM1's predicted bboxes on a copy of the composite as cyan boxes; save PNG per alert
Manifest JSON: alert_id, cam, gate_classification, vm1_predicted_class, vm1_predicted_bbox_a, vm1_predicted_bbox_b, IoU(VM1-bbox_a vs gate-bbox_a)
Run on 5-10 alert fixtures (suppressed alerts with frames on disk; gate_classification in {none})
out_of_scope: Modifying listener/pipeline.py or any production module
Touching camera-creds.env, .env, AGENTS.md, or any existing module
Integrating new VM1 output into the live pipeline
Wait for new vehicle alerts (~90 min) for backtest (use existing suppressed alerts with frames instead)

design_constraints: Body size: <=2,500 chars per card (local 35B worker ceiling).
ASCII-clean bodies only (no em-dash, smart quote, arrow, <= glyph).
Standalone module — does not import from listener/ or any infra module that touches the live pipeline at boot.
Vision model endpoint: VISION_LLM_URL from .env (already 127.0.0.1:8080, model Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-UD-Q4_K_XL).
Rate-limit: max 1 vision call per ~3s to avoid saturating local model (--sleep-between-calls knob).
Reversible: no production files touched; safe to archive and abandon if results are bad.

After US-095b: `cat data/backtest/manifest.json | jq '. | length'` returns >=5; `ls data/backtest/*/composite_with_vm1_bboxes.png | wc -l` matches manifest count
Operator reviews each PNG manually: does VM1's cyan bbox land on the moving subject (trees) or on the static parked object?
results_interpretation: If VM1's bboxes consistently land on the moving region (trees/foliage) and the class matches the moving region (not the parked car): the new prompt works. Next step is to consider integration into production (separate PRD, NOT this one).

If VM1's bboxes still land on the parked car: VM1 cannot tell motion from static given only 2 frames. The problem requires a different approach (e.g., cross-frame motion analysis in Python, or sending 4 frames). File a follow-up PRD.
If VM1's bboxes land somewhere random (neither motion nor parked car): prompt is too vague. Tighten prompt + retry.
